issues.description: The UML in problem_statement.md declares Ride with an attribute named 'abbreviation' (char). The solution's Ride class, however, declares the attribute as 'shortName' and provides a getter getShortName(). This naming mismatch between the UML/specification and the solution can confuse students about the expected getter name (getAbbreviation() vs getShortName()) and may cause tests or instructions that reference 'abbreviation' to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute name and getter consistent with the UML: either rename the field in the solution (and template) to 'abbreviation' and provide public char getAbbreviation(), or update the UML/problem statement to use 'shortName' and specify getShortName(). Ensure template, problem text, and solution use the same attribute name and corresponding getter.

issues.description: The UML/problem statement defines a Ride attribute named 'abbreviation' (char) but the solution implementation names the same attribute 'shortName' and provides getShortName(). This inconsistency between the problem/UML terminology ('abbreviation') and the code ('shortName' / getShortName) can confuse students who are instructed to implement attributes and getters exactly as in the UML and may look for getAbbreviation()/abbreviation. The template Ride.java is also empty (students will implement it according to the UML), so the mismatch between UML and solution introduces an unexpected naming divergence.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier consistent across artifacts. Rename the solution's field and accessor to match the UML: change 'shortName' to 'abbreviation' and 'getShortName()' to 'getAbbreviation()' (and update constructor parameter names accordingly), or alternatively update the UML/problem statement to use 'shortName' everywhere. Prefer aligning the code with the UML ('abbreviation') so students can implement getters exactly as specified.
